conceptZh: 兔子魔術師用力一揮魔杖，變出的燕子衝過頭飛出畫面又折回來，第二次輕輕一揮，燕子停在「燕」字上。
object: a cartoon magician rabbit in a purple top hat with a star-tipped wand, and a small glossy-feathered paper-craft swallow with a forked tail
morph: a swallow overshoots the stage, comes back, and settles as the strokes of 燕 with its four dots as tail feathers
creativeAngle: 衝過頭：兔子魔術師用力過猛，燕子飛過頭撞到舞台邊又彈回，第二次輕輕一揮才把筆畫排好，尾巴剛好是下面四點。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy with a locked frontal camera, bright and cheerful, no flashing. Setting: a clean solid pale-peach stage backdrop with a small striped curtain edge at the far left and right. The only on-screen text is one bold, saturated deep-teal Traditional Chinese glyph 燕, with its top 廿 part, the 北 in the middle, the small 口 in the heart and the four dots along the bottom, centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with margins. The lead is an original cartoon magician rabbit in a purple top hat with a star-tipped wand and long floppy ears; no real people. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the rabbit hops to center, winds up like a baseball pitcher and swings his wand with way too much power; a tiny forked-tail swallow whooshes out of the hat, shoots straight across the stage and vanishes off the right edge, the first spoken 燕 landing with the whoosh, while the rabbit spins on one foot and his ears wrap around his face. Moment two (1.8-3.4s): the swallow boomerangs back from the left, zips past again, bonks the curtain and drops a few feathers; the rabbit slaps his own forehead, then peeks out from between his ears. Moment three (3.4-5.0s): he takes a deep breath and gives a tiny, gentle flick; the second 燕 is spoken as the swallow floats in softly and settles, its body unfolding into the strokes of 燕 while the four tail feathers drop neatly into the four dots at the bottom, and the word 燕子 is spoken just as a little feather-flap puff of sparkles pops and the rabbit takes a bow. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 燕 is completely still, unobstructed and crisp; the rabbit stands to the side, tipping his top hat and doing a tiny happy hop, ears bouncing, never touching the strokes. Narration (off-screen only, warm Taiwanese Mandarin, slow, distinct, clear tones, no erhua): the voice says exactly 「燕、燕、燕子」, read as ㄧㄢˋ、ㄧㄢˋ、ㄧㄢˋ ㄗ˙, first utterance at about 0.5s, second at about 3.0s, the word at about 4.5s, then stop with no repeats and no extra speech. Only soft whoosh and a gentle chime under the voice, no background music. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter.

conceptZh: 調皮小老鼠想跟高處的小燕子擊掌，拚命把木板、方塊和四顆小石頭疊成搖搖晃晃的高塔，拉布拉多警長衝進來吹哨卻滑過頭，老鼠再放上一顆小瓜子，塔「轟」地倒下，散落的零件正好排成「燕」字，老鼠埋在乾草堆裡只露出眼睛，小燕子飛下來停在牠頭上。
object: a wobbly tower of barn junk: a wide flat plank with two pegs, two bracket-shaped boards, one small cube crate and four round pebbles, with a single sunflower seed as the last piece
morph: the toppling tower crashes and its pieces land as 燕: the pegged plank lands flat on top as 廿, the two bracket boards drop left and right as the 北 sides, the cube crate settles in the middle as 口, and the four pebbles roll into a neat row at the bottom as the four dots 灬
creativeAngle: 前一版是兔子魔術師揮棒變燕子的「發射」橋段；這次改成完全不同的「疊高再倒塌」肢體喜劇：老鼠為了搆到小燕子拚命疊塔，警長滑過頭讓塔晃得更兇，最後一顆小瓜子壓垮全部，倒塌的零件直接排成燕字，而「燕子」一詞由真的小燕子飛下來停在老鼠頭上來對應，三句語音都有畫面可看。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated slapstick clip, locked frontal camera, bright and cheerful, no flashing. Setting: a clean solid pale-butter-yellow barn wall with a plain wooden floor; a tiny forked-tail cartoon swallow sits on a high ledge at the top left corner, waving a wing. The only on-screen text is one bold, solid deep-blue Traditional Chinese glyph 燕 that forms at the crash, centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with margins. Lead: an original cheeky cartoon mouse, tiny, grey, with huge round ears and a permanent grin; no real people. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the mouse stares up at the swallow, points at it, holds up a paw for a high-five that is way out of reach, then stacks like lightning: four round pebbles, a small cube crate, two bracket-shaped boards, a wide plank with two pegs, the tower already leaning; the first spoken 燕 lands as the first piece hits the floor. Moment two (1.8-3.4s): a big friendly cartoon Labrador sheriff with a star badge charges in from the left blowing his whistle to stop this nonsense, skids straight past the tower and out the right edge in a cloud of dust; the gust makes the tower sway wildly while the mouse balances on tiptoe on top, arms windmilling. Moment three (3.4-5.0s): the mouse proudly sets one tiny sunflower seed on the very top, freeze for a beat, the tower creaks, then CRASH: with cartoon squash-and-stretch the whole stack tumbles and the pieces land as the strokes of 燕 - the pegged plank flat on top as 廿, the two bracket boards left and right as the sides of 北, the cube crate in the middle as 口, the four pebbles rolling into a neat row at the bottom as the four dots; the second 燕 is spoken as the pieces snap into place, and a puff of loose hay buries the mouse beside the glyph with only two blinking eyes poking out. Moment four (5.0-8.0s): the glyph 燕 stays perfectly still, crisp and unobstructed; the swallow swoops down in a smooth arc and perches on the mouse's head as the word 燕子 is spoken, the mouse pops up out of the hay, dizzy with swirly eyes, and finally gets its high-five from the swallow's wing, then does a tiny wobbly victory dance well away from the strokes. Narration (off-screen only, warm Taiwanese Mandarin, slow, distinct, clear tones, no erhua): the voice says exactly 「燕、燕、燕子」, read as ㄧㄢˋ、ㄧㄢˋ、ㄧㄢˋ ㄗ˙, first utterance at about 0.6s, second at about 4.3s, the word at about 5.4s, then stop with no repeats and no extra speech. Only light wooden clunks, a short whistle toot and a soft crash thump under the voice, no background music. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter.
